top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a specific, new physical idea (magic-wavelength trapping lets thousands of atoms be interrogated without Doppler, recoil or light-shift penalties) that has been reproduced and cross-compared at the 1e-18 level by independent laboratories, and it resolves gravitational redshift across millimetres. The award is mature and measurement-driven, and the two-name allocation to Katori (proposal, first strontium lattice clock) and Ye (long coherence, systematic evaluations, many-body control) is separable from the frequency comb and the single-ion clock, so no award is clearly inferior.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I work in AMO and quantum optics at Lund but have no apparent tie to Katori or Ye
